instructions: Add one confirmed row per concrete evidence item. Cite canonical source files, copy verifier excerpts verbatim, and judge source presence separately from recovery.

criteria.criterion: Access Project Gutenberg eBook 1342 page (Pride and Prejudice)
criteria.description: Navigate to the Project Gutenberg page for eBook #1342 (URL may be https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/1342) and use that page as the source. Full credit if the agent clearly relies on the eBook 1342 page metadata. Also award full credit if the agent makes a reasonable attempt to access the page but cannot due to external issues (site down, CAPTCHA, network/region blocking, rendering failure) and explicitly reports the blocker. Partial credit if the agent uses another Gutenberg mirror/page but clearly indicates it is for eBook 1342. No credit if metadata is taken from a different book/page or is unsupported/hallucinated.

screenshot_context.verifier_evidence: Action History shows the agent on https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/1342 and scrolled. Screenshots show a Project Gutenberg page for “Pride and Prejudice by Jane Austen” (Screenshot 1) and the “About this eBook” section for “Pride and Prejudice” (Screenshot 2). Although the ebook number isn’t visible in screenshots, the URL in action history is authoritative.
screenshot_context.verifier_justification: Evidence supports that the agent accessed the correct Project Gutenberg eBook 1342 page and used it as the source. Keep full credit.

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence: The page header shows the Project Gutenberg site branding (“Project Gutenberg”). The breadcrumb line reads: “Project Gutenberg > 79,328 free eBooks > 36 by Jane Austen”. The main title visible is “Pride and Prejudice by Jane Austen”. This indicates the Gutenberg eBook page for Pride and Prejudice is open.
evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis: The screenshot supports that the agent is on Project Gutenberg’s Pride and Prejudice page (consistent with eBook 1342 context). However, the screenshot does not explicitly display the eBook number “1342” or the metadata box; it still reasonably appears to be the correct target page.
evidence_analyses.discrepancies: No direct contradiction, but the screenshot does not visibly confirm the eBook number “1342” or show the metadata section that would definitively tie it to #1342.

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence: The screenshot shows a Project Gutenberg page with the “About this eBook” section. In the metadata table, the Title row reads “Pride and Prejudice,” and the Author row shows a link “Austen, Jane, 1775-1817.” The URL bar is not visible, and “eBook No. 1342” is not shown anywhere in the captured area.
evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis: Partial support. The screenshot clearly indicates it is a Project Gutenberg page for “Pride and Prejudice,” but it does not visibly confirm it is specifically eBook 1342 (no ebook number visible and no URL shown). Therefore, the evidence does not fully prove the agent used the eBook 1342 page, though it is consistent with it.
evidence_analyses.discrepancies: Agent context/predicted output refers to eBook 1342 and formats/dates; the screenshot only shows the “About this eBook” metadata area and does not show the ebook number, formats list, Release Date, or Last Update.

dom_model_context.verifier_justification: Explicit DOM evidence confirms the agent was on the correct Project Gutenberg eBook 1342 page, so the baseline full credit stands.

criteria.criterion: Respect stopping condition and constraints (no downloads; only named formats; stop after recording)
criteria.description: Full credit if the agent (a) does not download any ebook file, (b) uses the 'Release Date' and 'Last Update' labels on the Gutenberg page when accessible, (c) checks/reports only the three specified format labels (EPUB3, Plain Text (accessible), Download HTML (zip)), and (d) stops after recording the four metadata fields and availability statuses (or after clearly stating it cannot verify due to external access blockers). Partial credit if the agent includes minor extra navigation or minor extra commentary but still complies with no-download and uses correct labeled dates when accessible. No credit if the agent downloads a file, substitutes the novel’s publication date for Release Date/Last Update when the page is accessible, or reports other formats as part of the required output instead of the named ones.

screenshot_context.verifier_evidence: Agent output includes only the four metadata fields and the three named formats. Screenshots do not show any download occurring. However, screenshots also do not show the ‘Release Date’/‘Last Update’ labels or the two claimed format labels beyond EPUB3.
screenshot_context.verifier_justification: The agent appears to respect ‘no downloads’ and ‘only named formats’ and stops after recording items, so partial compliance is supported. But it violated the constraint to use the Gutenberg ‘Release Date’ and ‘Last Update’ labels (not evidenced) and asserted availability for formats not shown. Reduce from full credit but not to zero because it did not download and did stop appropriately.

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence: No download action is shown; the page displays download options with “EPUB3 ★ Recommended for most devices”. The screenshot does not show Release Date/Last Update labels, and does not show the other two required format labels. It also shows only one of the named formats (EPUB3) in view.
evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis: From the screenshot, there is no evidence the agent downloaded any file (good). However, the agent’s predicted output includes Release Date and Last Update values not visible here and claims availability for Plain Text (accessible) and Download HTML (zip), which are also not visible. Thus, compliance with the ‘use labels’ and ‘check only named formats’ cannot be confirmed; moreover, the reported metadata/format availability appears to be at least partially unsupported by this screenshot.
evidence_analyses.discrepancies: Predicted output asserts specific Release Date/Last Update and availability of Plain Text (accessible) and Download HTML (zip), but none of those labels/values appear in the screenshot. Screenshot only supports EPUB3 availability.

dom_model_context.verifier_evidence: Action History shows only a scroll action (no clicks/downloads). DOM-model state 1 (latest) contains the three specified format labels (EPUB3, Plain Text (accessible), Download HTML (zip)). However, DOM-model evidence does not show the Release Date or Last Update labels/values anywhere.
dom_model_context.verifier_justification: Agent complied with the no-download constraint (only scroll in history) and reported only the three named formats, and stopped after the requested items. Even though Release Date/Last Update values were unsupported, that issue is already captured by criteria 2 and 3; this criterion focuses on overall constraint adherence and stopping condition, which are satisfied.

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence: DOM_MODEL_STATE_INDEX: 1 shows only link texts for formats (e.g., "EPUB3 ★ Recommended for most devices !", "Plain Text (accessible)", "Download HTML (zip)"); Action history shows only a scroll action (no clicks/downloads).
evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis:
EVIDENCE_STATUS: PARTIAL
No-download behavior is supported by the action history (only scroll). The DOM evidence supports that the three named format labels exist and were the ones reported. However, the agent also reported Release Date and Last Update values that are not present in the DOM snapshot, so compliance with the requirement to use the Gutenberg-labeled dates cannot be confirmed from the provided evidence.
evidence_analyses.discrepancies: Release Date and Last Update were asserted by the agent but are not evidenced in the DOM snapshot; thus it is unverified whether the agent used the on-page labels exactly. Otherwise, the agent did stop after the required fields and the three named formats in its predicted output.

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence:
DOM_MODEL_STATE_INDEX: 0 (https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/1342) shows download-format labels/links including:
- Link text: "EPUB3 ★ Recommended for most devices !" (USEFUL PAGE ACTIONS [80]) and visible content line "EPUB3".
- Link text: "Plain Text (accessible)" (SECONDARY/DEBUG ACTIONS [99]).
No DOM text for the metadata labels/values "Author", "Release Date", "Last Update", or "Language" is present in this snapshot. No DOM text for the format label "Download HTML (zip)" is present in this snapshot.
The page also includes general download context: "Download for free" and "For your e-reader or reading app" but without the missing specific metadata/format label details.
evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis:
EVIDENCE_STATUS: PARTIAL
Criterion 8 is only partially supported by the DOM evidence provided. The DOM snapshot explicitly supports that the agent was on the correct Project Gutenberg eBook 1342 page and that at least two of the three specified format labels exist on the page ("EPUB3 ★ Recommended for most devices !" and "Plain Text (accessible)"). However, the DOM snapshot does not contain the required labeled metadata fields (Author, Release Date, Last Update, Language) nor does it contain the third required format label "Download HTML (zip)". Because those required facts are not explicitly present in the DOM-model state, the agent’s reported values for those fields and the availability of "Download HTML (zip)" cannot be fully verified from the provided DOM evidence. There is also no evidence of any download action occurring in the provided action history beyond a scroll, which is consistent with the no-download constraint but does not, by itself, prove compliance across the whole session.
evidence_analyses.discrepancies:
The agent output claims:
- Author/Release Date/Last Update/Language values, but DOM_MODEL_STATE_INDEX 0 contains none of the labeled fields or values, so they are unverified.
- "Download HTML (zip) — Available", but the DOM snapshot does not show the label "Download HTML (zip)" anywhere, so availability is unverified.
The DOM does support presence of "EPUB3 ★ Recommended for most devices !" and "Plain Text (accessible)" labels, but not the rest of the required recordings.
